• Click *Upload Image*.

• Download the PNG result. | This works best when the foreground object (the cat) stands out clearly against a contrasting backdrop. --- ### **Option 2 – Programmatic Removal Using Python (`rembg`)** If you prefer doing this locally or want batch processing, install the `rembg` package and run a short script. #### 1️⃣ Install Dependencies ```bash pip install -U pip setuptools wheel pip install rembg pillow tqdm ``` *(On Windows you may also need `git+https://github.com/danielgatis/rembg.git@master` if the PyPI version fails.)* #### 2️⃣ Run the Script Create a file called `cutout_cat.py`: ```python import sys from pathlib import Path from PIL import Image from rembg import remove import io def cut_background(input_path: str, output_path: str): # Load original image img_bytes = open(input_path, "rb").read() # Remove background new_img_data = remove(img_bytes) # Save as PNG (supports transparency) with open(output_path, "wb") as f: f.write(new_img_data) if __name__ == "__main__": if len(sys.argv) != 3: print("Usage: python cutout_cat.py input.jpg output.png") sys.exit(1) inp, outp = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] cut_background(inp, outp) print(f"Background removed → {outp}") ``` Run it from the command line: ```bash python cutout_cat.py cat.jpeg cat_no_bg.png ``` After execution, `cat_no_bg.png` will contain only the cat silhouette over a transparent canvas. --- ### Tips & Troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | Background still visible around edges | Try increasing the confidence threshold: `new_img_data = remove(img_bytes, thresh=0.8)` | | Cat’s fur looks jagged | Post‑process with a soft blur filter or manually refine mask in GIMP / Photoshop. | | Very complex backgrounds | Consider manual masking first, then feed the rough mask into `rembg`. | Let me know if you'd like help setting up the environment or tweaking the results!
